newsitem.title: KENYA: Youths clash outside Kenya parliament.
newsitem.headline: Youths clash outside Kenya parliament.

text.p: Police inside Kenya's parliament compound fired on Thursday to disperse youths supporting opposition parties who clashed outside with youths backing the ruling party, witnesses said.

Fifty youths shouting slogans in support of the ruling Kenya African National Union (KANU) and 50 youths allied with opposition parties hurled rocks at each other on the road outside the parliament building in the centre of the capital.
Police fired in the air to disperse opposition supporters but it was unclear if they were live ammunition or blanks. Three people including a policeman were lightly hurt by flying stones.
"We are from (opposition party leader Kenneth) Matiba's army and we want political dialogue. We are not paid to come here," one youth grasping two rocks told Reuters.
The incident, which disrupted rush hour traffic in the area around parliament, ended after a couple of hours when riot police chased the youths away from the compound.
The clashes were the latest in a row between an opposition-backed alliance pressing for constitutional reforms before presidential and parliamentary elections and KANU.
Opposition party parliamentarians inside the parliament building accused KANU of deliberately bringing the youths to parliament to harass them as they entered or left the building.

"Some youths clearly organised by the ruling party are harrassing opposition MP's trying to drive into parliament or out of parliament. These are hired thugs who will not move until they are paid," said Paul Muite, a leading member of the unregistered Safina party.
"This was just a stupid incident organised by two groups of MPs, one from the ruling party and one from the opposition. It was just an act of stupidity," said Boy Juma Boy, the government chief whip.

KANU said on Wednesday it would not discuss constitutional reforms with the National Convention Executive Council (NCEC), an alliance of opposition-backed groups campaigning for reforms before a general election due later this year, because it was a non-elected body.
The NCEC said it had a popular mandate for dialogue and plans a rally in the Indian Ocean city of Mombasa on Saturday.
